from._: Which clip each frame was cut from, at 2 fps, so they can be made again: ffmpeg -i <clip> -vf fps=2 f%04d.png

note: Five settled frames, one per configuration, pulled from the clips Al
recorded of each slot a part opens: gun upper rail slot, gun red dot optic
slot, gun kill flash slot, gun grip mount slot, gun rear grip slot. The
upper-rail and rear-grip-mount states appear in two clips each and agree to
a third of a grey level, which is how we know they are settled.
These were recorded in a later session than the base frame the chips and
the artwork in data/gunsmith-ar-57.json came from, and the game rests the
fan a few pixels differently between sessions -- the camera is about 1.7%
wider here, so the weapon is drawn 15px shorter and the chips sit up to 12
pixels off their recorded base positions. No transform explains it (a
least-squares affine still leaves 6px), so the two are not reconciled: each
layout is internally consistent, which is what the page draws, and the
difference is smaller than the reflow the game itself does when a slot
opens. The base frame is not re-cut from this session because the rifle has
a charm hanging off it here, which would end up in the artwork.

clips.why: The modular grip's card prints Grip Mount under Conflicting Slots and this clip was cut believing that mattered. It cannot: the mount is opened by a DIFFERENT rear grip, so no build has both. The conflict is out of the rules and out of this layout, which is what was really watched -- nothing was removed here, because nothing was there to remove.
